Definition: from Latin (" august "); Augustus, a title of the Roman emperor:--Augustus.
BiblicalUsage: Caesar Augustus decreed that all the world should be taxed, and his decree sent Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, where Christ was born. The word is the emperor's title, and it appears only here.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the emperor's decree was God's instrument, because the man who ruled the world moved a young couple to the town where the Messiah had to be born.
RelatedPeople: Caesar Augustus; Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus
